change_summary: The paper has been withdrawn at the editor's request. The reason given is that the indoor temperature records had been processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, so the reported results cannot be relied on, and the full text and PDF were replaced by the withdrawal statement. The stored paper's main results, a 2.1 °C lower mean daily peak indoor temperature and 41% fewer hours above 28 °C in green-roofed flats, come from those indoor records, so the whole paper's results can't be relied on.
evaluation: Your Data and methods section cites Okafor et al. [14] as the source of the 2.1 °C green-roof cooling value you set in your model, and the stored paper reports that 2.1 °C lower daily peak indoor temperature. The withdrawal statement says the indoor temperature records had been processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, so the reported results cannot be relied on, which touches this use of the 2.1 °C value. Your Discussion also cites [14] for the 2.1 °C reduction your green-roof result scales with, and that use is touched too. The impact on your draft is high, because the model's key parameter comes from the withdrawn paper.
recommendation: The draft sets its model's green-roof cooling value to 2.1 °C citing Okafor et al. [14], and the paper has been withdrawn because the indoor temperature records had been processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, so the reported results cannot be relied on. The impact on your draft is high, because the draft takes its key model parameter from the withdrawn paper's results. Raise this with your co-authors or supervisor before editing the text, since the model itself depends on the value. Then replace the value, re-run the model, and re-check the Discussion and the citation.
